title: The Difference Between Diamond and Immortal

creativeDirection.objective: Explain why high-elo VALORANT performance depends on round-winning decisions, not aim alone.
creativeDirection.audience: Competitive VALORANT players from Diamond aiming to improve toward Immortal.
creativeDirection.concept: A dark esports documentary combining authentic user-recorded VALORANT ACE/multikill footage with original tactical motion graphics to explain the contrast between isolated duels and coordinated round-winning decisions.

visualSystem.typography: Bold condensed-feeling editorial sans serif, short uppercase headlines, compact technical labels and clean subtitles.
visualSystem.composition: Editorial copy anchored left, animated tactical diagrams and target geometry on the right; full-frame motion graphics for transitions and the final title.
visualSystem.lighting: Near-black backgrounds with restrained red threat lighting, cool blue team-information accents and sharp white highlights.
visualSystem.textureAndMaterials: Fine grid lines, radar traces, soft grain-like particles, luminous vector strokes and clean tactical-map geometry.

creativeDirection.motionLanguage: Every chapter contains moving paths, shifting target geometry, animated markers, pulsing zones or kinetic type. Use hard match cuts and short whoosh accents; no static slide sequence. Tactical graphics are explicitly illustrative, never presented as captured VALORANT gameplay.
creativeDirection.soundDirection: Confident English narration from the built-in US English Kokoro voice, original rhythmic electronic score, music ducked beneath speech, restrained transition sweeps, low impact accents on the mistake and successful execution, and a final tonal resolve.
assumptions: The built-in US English voice is used; the exact voice timbre will be judged from the rendered audio.
Seven user-owned VALORANT ACE/multikill clips are supplied and mapped across the six chapters; their footage is used as authentic gameplay, while explanatory tactical graphics remain illustrative.
rightsAndFactualConstraints: Do not use VALORANT gameplay, agent models, official logos, game UI or third-party music without supplied or verified rights.
Label all map, reticle and team-position graphics as explanatory visualizations, not authentic match footage.
Use only original vector artwork and the repository's generated audio fixtures.
User-owned gameplay clips are recorded by the project owner and are not represented as third-party licensed footage.

shots.purpose: Hook Diamond players with the frustration of being mechanically strong but stuck.
shots.visual: An abstract red pressure corridor closes around a moving reticle; the frame resolves into the question WHY DO GOOD PLAYERS GET STUCK? This is a designed visual metaphor, not gameplay.
shots.framing: Editorial left-aligned headline with a large right-side pressure tunnel and central reticle.
shots.cameraMovement: The tunnel graphic pushes forward, reticle drifts off-centre, and perspective lines draw toward a threat point.
shots.onScreenText: WHY DO GOOD PLAYERS GET STUCK?
shots.transition: Hard cut on the reticle center to the next scene's target geometry.
shots.audio: Score enters with a low pulse; short original whoosh on the opening hit.
shots.action: Pressure lines close around a drifting reticle, then the question headline resolves.
shots.visualProgression: Start: open pressure corridor. Development: lines converge and the reticle drifts off-centre. End: the headline lands as the visual pressure point.

shots.purpose: Show that a clean aim duel is only one part of winning a round.
shots.visual: A reticle sweeps toward a concentric target, a tracer draws across frame, and an impact ring expands then disappears.
shots.framing: Left editorial statement; right macro target geometry and reticle.
shots.cameraMovement: Reticle slides and overshoots before correcting; target rings expand in a brief slow-motion beat.
shots.transition: Cut from the expanding target ring into a top-down tactical map.
shots.audio: Electronic pulse continues under narration; a restrained hit accent marks the target contact.
shots.visualMethod: Motion graphics / target animation with gameplay insert if approved footage is available
shots.action: The reticle tracks toward a target, tracer connects, and the impact ring expands then clears.
shots.visualProgression: Start: target and reticle are separated. Development: reticle sweeps, corrects, and the tracer reaches the target. End: impact ring expands and becomes the map transition.

shots.purpose: Explain positioning, information, utility and trade spacing.
shots.visual: A top-down abstract map appears; teammate nodes move into crossfire positions while route lines draw and enemy information pulses.
shots.framing: Left title and concise copy; right tactical map with blue allied nodes and red threat markers.
shots.cameraMovement: Routes draw across the map, teammate markers shift into position, and an information pulse expands around a revealed threat.
shots.transition: Hard cut on a red enemy pulse to the isolated-peek warning.
shots.audio: Score builds; subtle whoosh at the chapter change.
shots.visualMethod: Animated tactical map / motion graphics with footage insert where available
shots.action: Teammate nodes move into crossfire positions as routes draw and threat information pulses.
shots.visualProgression: Start: map with separated team nodes. Development: routes draw and players reposition into coordinated spacing. End: threat pulse reveals the next decision.

shots.purpose: Make the cost of an unnecessary solo duel immediately legible.
shots.visual: One blue player path pushes alone into a red danger zone; enemy threat lines converge, the motion stops, and BAD DECISION = LOST ROUND appears.
shots.framing: Left editorial headline; right map, isolated player marker and red warning cross.
shots.cameraMovement: A single route advances, then freezes as the danger zone expands and a warning cross snaps into place.
shots.transition: Impact cut from the red cross into a coordinated blue route.
shots.audio: Music briefly dips; low impact at the freeze; narration remains clear.
shots.visualMethod: Illustrative tactical animation with authentic gameplay footage only if available
shots.action: A lone player route pushes into a danger zone as threat lines converge, then the action freezes on the exposed position.
shots.visualProgression: Start: player is approaching an angle. Development: the route enters the danger zone and threat lines converge. End: movement freezes with the warning state visible.

shots.purpose: Show a coordinated alternative: utility, space, trading and execution.
shots.visual: Two routes converge, a utility radius expands, and three allied markers enter together while the site is isolated.
shots.framing: Left statement; right map with converging routes, utility radius and coordinated markers.
shots.cameraMovement: Paths draw in staggered sequence; utility expands; team markers arrive on the beat and hold a crossfire.
shots.transition: Match cut from the final team marker into the central final emblem.
shots.audio: Score reaches its strongest pulse; a controlled impact marks the team convergence.
shots.visualMethod: Tactical motion graphics with authorized gameplay footage
shots.action: Team routes converge in staggered timing, utility expands and allied markers establish a crossfire.
shots.visualProgression: Start: routes and team positions are separated. Development: utility expands and routes converge. End: the team holds coordinated space.

shots.purpose: Resolve the opening question with a memorable competitive principle.
shots.visual: The tactical lines collapse into a red-and-white geometric emblem; the final message locks into place over a slow luminous orbit.
shots.framing: Clean centered final title with an animated emblem behind it.
shots.cameraMovement: Rings rotate in opposite directions and settle as the final words arrive.
shots.transition: Fade to black on the final beat.
shots.audio: Score resolves; a short original chime lands under the final line.
shots.action: Tactical geometry resolves into an emblem while the final message arrives and holds.
shots.visualProgression: Start: tactical paths converge. Development: geometry collapses into the emblem and the final line locks in. End: motion settles and the message holds before fade.

acceptanceCriteria: Final output is a 1920×1080, 16:9 H.264 MP4 with a 60-second duration, within the repository's supported 60-second project limit.
English narration is generated from the approved script, remains intelligible, and is accompanied by word-aligned captions.
Every scene contains purposeful animated motion and the six chapters use distinct compositions; the result must not read as a slideshow.
Music is ducked beneath narration and transitions/impact accents are synchronized to the visual events.
No synthetic visual is described or implied to be authentic VALORANT gameplay; tactical diagrams are clearly illustrative.
The actual rendered MP4 is inspected for pacing, motion, caption timing, audio balance and technical integrity before delivery.

renderStrategy.rationale: This legacy VALORANT explainer combines user-owned gameplay clips with explanatory 2D tactical overlays and narration; its current project is authored for the ProjectVideo schema. Its known visual limitations remain an explicit creative-QA concern.
renderStrategy.fallback: If editorial footage-led cutting, reframing or kinetic camera work cannot be achieved in ProjectVideo, build a dedicated custom Remotion edit and keep tactical graphics as supporting inserts.
